Stage 1 appeal  If your appeal is about (1) urgent or emergency care (where your doctor believes a delay in making a decision could put your life, health or ability to regain full function at serious risk, or could cause you severe pain), (2) an admission, (3) the availability of care, or (4) your continued stay ina facility and you have not been discharged, you, your doctor or other authorized representative can request a fast review. To do this, call the National Clinical Appeal Unit expedited appeal toll-free number at  1-888-408-7485. You can also fax your request to 1-860-754-0068.  The National Clinical Appeal Unit will document phone requests in writing. We will give you a decision within 36 hours after receipt of your request if your plan provides two levels of appeal or 72 hours after receipt of your request if your plan provides one level of appeal. If your appeal is about your continued stay in a facility to treat a substance use disorder and you have not been discharged, we'll give you a decision within 24 hours after receipt of your request. You may also request an expedited external review at the same time as your expedited Stage 1 appeal.  For all other Stage 1 appeals, we will give you a decision within 10 calendar days after receipt of your request.  As part of a Stage 1 appeal of a denial based on medical necessity, you (or your provider with your consent) may also ask to speak with the Medical Director who made the initial coverage denial.  Stage 2 appeal  If you do not agree with the Stage 1 appeal decision, you may request a Stage 2 appeal if your plan provides a second level of appeal, or you may be able to request an external review if your plan does not provide a second level of appeal. Your Stage 1 appeal decision letter will tell you what additional appeal rights you may have.  External review  If your appeal results in our continued denial of payment or coverage based on medical necessity, or we do not give you a timely appeal decision, you can request an external review of your claim by an independent third party, who will review the denial and issue a final decision. The external review process is not available for denials based on eligibility or a plan exclusion or limitation not related to medical necessity.  You or your authorized representative (who could be your doctor) have the option to appeal directly to an independent review organization if we have denied your non-formulary drug exception request. You can request an urgent appeal if your situation is considered by law to be urgent. You, your doctor, or an authorized representative who can act on your behalf (such as a caregiver or attorney) can file your appeal.  How long will it take to review my appeal?  For standard appeals:  We will review your appeal and make a decision within 15 days or 30 days of receiving your appeal, depending on how many levels of review are required by your plan. This gives us time to fully review your request and coordinate with your doctor.  For urgent appeals: If your request meets legal requirements for an urgent review, a decision will be made within 72 hours. Your doctor will be notified, and a decision letter will be mailed to you.

For standard appeals:  We will review your appeal and make a decision within 15 days or 30 days of receiving your appeal, depending on how many levels of review are required by your plan. This gives us time to fully review your request and coordinate with your doctor.  For urgent appeals: If your request meets legal requirements for an urgent review, a decision will be made within 72 hours. Your doctor will be notified, and a decision letter will be mailed to you.  I've submitted my appeal. What happens next?  Your plan will review the decision and respond in writing. If your appeal is denied or if you don’t receive a timely decision, you may have the right to ask for an external review by an independent third party. The external review can take place at the same time as your appeal if your situation is urgent.
